FalkorDB perfRunsTrends

Trends

Both images' own numbers per row, run after run (candidate solid, baseline dashed; a red or green dot is a run that called the row a regression or improvement; a vertical line, a new baseline), so a release that carries a change does not hide it. The newest 90 runs per scope.

Scope:

fuzz · main

What counts as a regression: The control epoch (4 runs: candidate, baseline, baseline, candidate) checks invariants. A data invariant (writes add up, upsert edges complete) or a crash on the candidate only is a regression at once; a timing invariant (no freeze: no PING later than 500 ms while a plain server answered within 100 ms; no timeouts while waiting; writers don't starve; quiet graphs stay fast; requests drain; no error replies) counts only when one more pair repeats it. Graph build at scale 0.25: a node or edge phase regresses past 1.5x and by more than 500 ms, a wiring query past 1.5x and by more than 2 ms, in the first runs and again in an extra pair. Info, not gated: an invariant broken on both sides, a break that did not repeat.

ldbc · main

What counts as a regression: LDBC SNB interactive queries, each image its own server. A query's p50 or p95 latency regresses past 2x and by more than a floor (p50 0.5 ms, p95 2 ms), confirmed by a re-run of that query on both sides. At once: different rows returned, or a request the candidate failed (error, timeout, server down) that the baseline finished. Info, not gated: a crossing the re-run did not repeat, a query that fails on both sides.

micro-hw · main

What counts as a regression: Each benchmark query runs 2 times a side on one C4 VM; a row is one query (reads or writes) and one metric, compared by medians. It regresses when it rises past the threshold by more than the floor (or past the steep ratio by more than the smaller floor), both candidate readings sit above both baseline readings, and a re-run repeats it; a query that errors on the candidate only is a regression at once. Rust: instructions +10% and 250,000; cycles +10% and 20,000,000, or 1.8x and 250,000; branch misses +25% and 12,000, or 2.8x and 2,000; L2 misses +25% and 225,000, or 3.0x and 15,000; allocated bytes +10% and 65,536, or 8.0x and 4,096. C (either side): instructions +10% and 1,300,000; cycles +10% and 270,000; branch misses +25% and 40,000; L2 misses +25% and 665,000, or 3.1x and 15,000; allocated bytes +10% and 3,100,000, or 8.0x and 4,096. Info, not gated: a crossing the re-run did not repeat, a query that errors on both sides, each class's median ratio and sign count.

pokec · main

What counts as a regression: The Pokec dataset, read-only and 5% writes, 3 runs a side. A latency row (p50, p95, p99 of each query and of all queries) regresses past 1.3x and past a floor (p50 1 ms, p95 5 ms, p99 15 ms), in the first pass and again in a re-run of 2 runs a side; under writes only all queries and a read query's p50 gate. Throughput regresses when it drops past 1.3x in both passes. At once, no re-run: a run that did not finish (it took 3x the other side's slowest run, or its server stopped), an error reply; a query that times out in 2 runs, or a PING over 1,000 ms in 2 runs that is past 1.3x the baseline's. Info, not gated: a crossing the re-run did not repeat, a failure on both sides, a freeze as long on the baseline.

Moved (crossed a gate in at least one of these 2 runs):

soak-a · main

What counts as a regression: Each scenario runs once a side. An op's p50 regresses past 2x and by more than 2 ms, its throughput below 0.7x, a scenario's setup wall time past 1.5x and by more than 5 s; each only when a re-run of the scenario, order swapped, crosses again. An op is compared once the baseline has 200 samples; its latency once the candidate has 20 too. At once, no re-run: a correctness check broken on the candidate only, a crash, a scenario that did not complete; a latency or resource check counts only when every run pair repeats it. Info, not gated: a p99 shift (past 2x and 10 ms, with 1,000 baseline samples), a check broken on both sides, and a known flaky check while its issue is open: #3095.

soak-b · main

What counts as a regression: Each scenario runs once a side. An op's p50 regresses past 2x and by more than 2 ms, its throughput below 0.7x, a scenario's setup wall time past 1.5x and by more than 5 s; each only when a re-run of the scenario, order swapped, crosses again. An op is compared once the baseline has 200 samples; its latency once the candidate has 20 too. At once, no re-run: a correctness check broken on the candidate only, a crash, a scenario that did not complete; a latency or resource check counts only when every run pair repeats it. Info, not gated: a p99 shift (past 2x and 10 ms, with 1,000 baseline samples), a check broken on both sides, and a known flaky check while its issue is open: #3095.
